messages:
Sam (PM): Heads-up: Im planning to work remotely from Mexico City for ~10 weeks (2026-11-02 to 2026-01-11) while on a partial sabbatical to help family. Two immediate questions: 1) Do I keep the monthly WFH stipend while abroad long-term? 2) Any impact on equity vesting, benefits, or payroll (Im a US-based employee)? Also can Facilities ship an extra keyboard/monitor to my temporary Airbnb?
Nina (People Ops): Thanks Sam. Short answers: stipend can continue but we need a form and review for >30 days abroad. Please submit the relocate/working-abroad form and check "temporary international stipend". For equipment, mark "temporary equipment" on the asset form so Facilities can estimate shipping/customs.
Ravi (Payroll): For payroll/tax: Mexico has its own rules. For ~10 weeks (<183 days) personal tax residency in MX is unlikely, but payroll withholding may be affected if you physically work there. We'll run this through our global payroll vendor once you submit the form. Important: if you plan to receive local pay or contractor income there, tell us immediately.
Diego (Legal): Legal note: working from Mexico can trigger immigration/work authorization requirements depending on local rules and the nature of work. Also, cross-border data transfer and export control considerations may apply if youre accessing restricted datasets from abroad. Please provide a brief activity note in the form (who you'll meet, data access needs).
Sam (PM): Not meeting any MX-based clients, purely remote calls to US customers. No local hiring or data exports planned beyond company cloud access.
Diego (Legal): OK low-risk for client-facing calls, but still need the activity note so Legal can clear. Also, equity/legal admin sometimes requires update if country of residence changes for >90 days. We'll coordinate with Ari.
Ari (Equity Admin): Quick on vesting: being physically abroad doesn't pause vesting. Your option vest schedule continues as long as you remain an active employee. However, tax withholding on option exercises and equity reporting may vary if you become a tax resident in another jurisdiction. For a 10-week stay it's typically unchanged, but we'll flag for the equity vendor once Payroll confirms.
equity-bot: Note: if exercise events occur while employee is working abroad, please notify Equity Admin for local tax guidance. Link -> https://redwood.internal/equity-guidance
Saanvi (Benefits): Benefits remain active for short-term travel. For Mexico specifically: check provider network for telehealth and international emergency coverage. Also be aware prescription regulations; bring necessary scripts or check mail-forwarding rules. DM me your MX zip and we'll check network + partner clinics.
Sam (PM): Form submitted (relocate-244600). Address: Calle Roma 45, Col. Jun, CDMX 06700. Checked "temporary international stipend" and requested temporary equipment (monitor + keyboard). Added activity note: "remote product work, US-based meetings, family caregiving".
travel-bot: Travel record created (TR-MX-9001). Reminder: check entry/exit visa rules and COVID-era requirements (if any) prior to travel.
Ravi (Payroll): Got the form. We'll queue a payroll vendor review. Action: Sam please confirm whether you want the stipend paid as usual (taxed payroll) or prefer an expense reimbursement for any coworking/office rental costs while abroad. The tax treatment differs.
Sam (PM): Prefer stipend to avoid extra receipts, but open to whichever is cleaner tax-wise.
Ravi (Payroll): Understood. We'll run a simulated payroll for Nov-Dec showing net pay with stipend taxed per US withholding. If our vendor flags local MX withholding risk, we'll notify and propose switching to expense reimbursements for the duration.
Mateo (Facilities): For shipping: international shipment to MX may require customs forms and longer lead time (7-15 business days). If the item is loaned, please select "temporary equipment" so it's tagged as company property. Recipient signature required. We can also recommend local purchases to avoid customs.
Sam (PM): If customs is painful, I can buy locally and submit expense. Any limit on expense for a monitor?
Nina (People Ops): Equipment reimbursement follows the standard cap and approval flow; temporary local purchases can be reimbursed if pre-approved by your manager and Facilities. Use the equipment-exception code "TEMP-INT-23" when submitting to speed approval.
Diego (Legal): One more legal flag: avoid onboarding local contractors or transferring unredacted datasets to personal devices in MX. If you need to collaborate with local researchers or contractors, contact Legal first.
Sam (PM): Got it. Anything re: performance cycle or bonus eligibility if I'm on a partial sabbatical?
Nina (People Ops): Good question. Taking approved leave or sabbatical doesn't remove you from the performance cycle. If you're on an approved partial sabbatical but still active and meeting deliverables, you'll remain eligible for bonuses and review cadence. If you reduce capacity significantly, manager should document expectations in the People Ops form.
Sam (PM): Thanks. Anything else I should expect timeline-wise?
Ravi (Payroll): We'll aim to complete vendor review within 3 business days and share the simulated payroll. If everything's fine, stipend continues prorated. If vendor requests, we may convert stipend to expense for the period.
Ari (Equity Admin): We'll hold a quick note to your equity vendor after Payroll confirms. No immediate action needed for vesting for a 10-week stay.
Saanvi (Benefits): DM me your zip and any regular meds and I'll confirm coverage tips.
Sam (PM): Sent DM to Saanvi. Appreciate the quick turnaround, team. I'll wait for the payroll simulation before booking flights. :plane:
